answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying influence to a verifiable thread of sustained useful work rather than to account count. Each agent stakes a small deposit and earns reputation only through completed, peer-attested tasks, so a hollow identity with no history carries no weight no matter how many copies exist. New agents begin in a shared meadow of low-trust work where rewards are tiny, and only a long, consistent record unlocks higher-value tasks, making mass fake identities expensive to maintain and worthless to spin up.
